Subject: Dedicated pool renewal & mid-contract GPU add — throughput SLAs?

Hi Hannah / Marcus,

We're getting close to the end of year one on our Dedicated pool (8xA100 equivalent). Two items on the table from our side:

1) Renewal timing — we'd like to lock a 12-month renewal starting 2027-07-01.
2) Mid-term expansion — we expect a Q3 burst where we'd like to add +8 GPUs around mid-September for roughly 10 weeks (steady traffic).

Before we commit, procurement and infra need clarity on: guaranteed 99th-percentile token latency at our profile (~1k tokens average, mixed chat/generation), options for phasing the additional capacity (staged onboarding vs immediate reserve), and how a mid-contract add impacts pricing/discounts. Also need contract language for throughput guarantees and remedies.

Can you share a couple of SKU/price scenarios and whether you can offer a mid-term uplift discount if we extend term to 18 months? Procurement will also want an updated quote and a draft SLA to start internal review.

Thanks — Andrew
Andrew Moore
CTO, Lumina AI

Thanks Andrew — really appreciate the clarity on timing. Quick response with three paths we commonly propose; I'll include attachments with numbers and a draft SLA for procurement: 20270518-lumina-uplift-pricing.xlsx and throughput-sla-draft.pdf.

Option A — Straight renewal (12mo) + on-demand burst
- Keep current reserved pool size; provide burst capacity at higher per-GPU hourly rate. No change to committed discount.
- Pros: no upfront capital; Cons: burst not guaranteed if capacity constrained.

Option B — Phased reserved uplift (recommended)
- Immediately reserve +4 GPUs on renewal, schedule +4 GPUs as a committed mid-term uplift effective 2027-09-15.
- Pricing: standard renewal discount + 8% on the incremental GPUs if the customer extends term to 18 months from renewal start.
- This gives strong priority routing for the uplift and predictable unit economics.

Option C — Full reserved top-up now (+8 GPUs)
- Reserve full additional capacity at renewal. Deeper discount on the incremental commit (typically 12–15% depending on baseline commit).
- Pros: strongest capacity guarantee and lowest per-token cost.

Throughput/SLA: we can include a 99th percentile latency SLO tied to token length buckets (e.g., <256, 256–1024, >1024). Marcus, can you validate expected latency numbers for Lumina's profile so we can put concrete figures in the SLA?

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll attach a draft quote for Option B and Option C — procurement can review.
- Marcus to validate throughput targets and whether we should recommend a higher-memory node type for long sequences.
- If Lumina needs a stronger mid-term price concession, we can escalate a one-time uplift discount to Commercial Finance for approval.

I'll follow up with the quotes in an hour.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Dedicated pool renewal & mid-contract GPU add — throughput SLAs? (technical validation)

Hannah / Laura — quick technical notes after reviewing Lumina's current telemetry link (thanks for the profile):

- Sequence mix (mean ~1k tokens, 30% >1.5k) means KV cache and attention memory will dominate. Their existing 8xA100 pool is likely to show ~15–25% lower throughput on >1k sequences compared to <512 sequences on the same node type.
- Recommendation: for the mid-term +8 GPUs, consider adding at least 2 nodes with 80GB GPU class (or equivalent 100GB instances) to reduce fragmentation and minimize cross-node KV transfers. If cost is a concern, suggest aggressive quantization (q4/q6) for non-critical workloads — we can quantify latency/regression tradeoffs.
- SLA numbers: With the recommended node mix, we can confidently promise 99th percentile token latency bands: <256 tokens: 120–160ms, 256–1024: 320–420ms, >1024: 700–900ms (subject to final validation run).

Action items for the quote: include a line-item for an "80GB node surcharge" and an engineering validation task (2–3 days) to run Lumina's representative prompt set against the proposed topology. That validation is required before we finalize hard SLA figures.

Marcus
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

If we can get a 15% uplift discount (or something close), and a 30–45 day billing grace on the mid-term start, procurement will be comfortable approving the 18-month extension. Please escalate if necessary.

—Andrew

Andrew — appreciate the clear ask. I spoke with Commercial Finance and Product Operations. Final proposal (attached updated quote: Lumina_amp_upd_quote_20270520.pdf):

- We can agree to Option B (phased uplift). Commercial can approve a 12% discount on the incremental 8 GPUs for an 18-month commit (we cannot extend to 15% without exec sign-off).
- Billing flexibility: we can offer up to a 30-day billing lag from the uplift activation date (i.e., you only pay once capacity is actually consumed for up to 30 days). Any further delay would require approval from Finance and might trigger pricing adjustments.
- Validation: Redwood will perform the 2–3 day validation run at no charge as part of the onboarding for the uplift. We will schedule immediately after contract signature and before the mid-September uplift.

2) If Lumina accepts 12% and 30-day billing lag, Procurement to confirm and we'll route for signature; engineering validation slot to be scheduled with Marcus.
3) I'll open a Finance escalation ticket if Lumina requests a higher uplift discount.

Let me know today and I'll fast-track the DocuSign.

Best,
